name: Shelemiah
overview: Shelemiah was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, specifically a descendant of Aaron, serving during the time of Nehemiah. He is uniquely noted as a priest appointed by Nehemiah, highlighting his role in the religious leadership of Israel. His priestly status underscores his connection to the Levitical priesthood and the responsibilities therein.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelemiah means 'YHWH pays back' or 'He restores peace offering of YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to God's provision and restoration. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 13:13 and was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual implications.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shelemiah as a descendant of Aaron, which situates him within the Levitical priestly lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are explicitly recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shelemiah's significance lies in his appointment by Nehemiah as a priest, which demonstrates the restoration and organization of the priesthood during the post-exilic period. His role as a descendant of Aaron affirms the continuity of the Aaronic priesthood amidst Israel's return from exile. This appointment reflects God's ongoing provision for proper worship and leadership within the community of Israel.
